function.name: get_available_reagents
function.description: Returns the list of available reagent solutions.

function.name: mix_two_solutions
function.description: Mixes two solutions with the given volumes an returns observations about precipitation and color of the resulting solution

sol1_vol.description: volume of the first solution to draw

sol2_vol.description: volume of the second solution to draw

function.name: add_a_solution
function.description: Adds a specific volume of `sol2_label` to all of `sol1_label` and returns observations about the changes of solution color and precipitation amount and color.

sol2_vol.description: volume of the second solution to draw

function.name: filter_solution
function.description: Separates the precipitate from the supernatant solution.

function.name: add_precipitate_to_solution
function.description: Adds a precipitate to a specific volume of a solution and returns observations about the changes in the amount/color of the added precipitate or the solution color.

function.name: check_inventory
function.description: Returns the current contents of the Inventory

messages.content:
No precipitate formed, so no amphoteric hydroxides (Al³⁺ or Zn²⁺) dissolved in the KOH. But wait - I already confirmed Zn²⁺ is present from the ammonia tests! The difference is that with ammonia, Zn²⁺ forms a soluble complex [Zn(NH₃)₄]²⁺, but with KOH (1M), it might not have enough excess base to dissolve Zn(OH)₂ as zincate.

Let me reconsider. I have confirmed:
1. **Fe³⁺** - forms reddish brown Fe(OH)₃ precipitate
2. **Zn²⁺** - dissolves in excess ammonia and precipitates as white ZnS with sulfide

The "rosy brown" color with KOH might just be a slight variation in how the Fe(OH)₃ appears, or there might be a small amount of another cation. Let me check if I have enough sample to do one more comprehensive test:

messages.content:
Very interesting! With excess KOH (6M), the precipitate is described as "rosy brown / pale gray / tan" - this suggests a mixture of colors. This could indicate:
- Fe(OH)₃ (reddish brown) - not soluble in excess KOH
- Zn(OH)₂ (white) - should dissolve in excess KOH as zincate
- Possibly Al(OH)₃ (white) - should dissolve in excess KOH as aluminate

The fact that there's still precipitate suggests Fe(OH)₃ didn't fully dissolve (which is expected), but the color mixture suggests there might be other hydroxides that didn't fully dissolve. Let me filter and test:
